instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the lower middle.
Cut the meat off the lamb bones and keep the bones. Trim off any big pieces of fat and cut the meat into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Season it with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in two batches, about 5 minutes a batch, and transfer it to a bowl.

Turn the heat down to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until the onions are soft and browned at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in 2 cups of water a little at a time, stirring so there are no lumps. Add 2 tsp minced fresh thyme and 1 tsp of the salt and bring it to a simmer.
Add the lamb bones, then the lamb and any juices from the bowl. Cover and bake for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch cubes.
Take the pot out of the oven and lay the potatoes on top of the meat. Cover and bake for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender and a knife slides easily into a potato.
Skim the fat off the top with a spoon and take out the bones. Stir in 3 tbsp chopped parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the stew into bowls. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days.
method_notes: Lead is America's Test Kitchen (4.5 from 32): lamb shoulder with its bones, onions browned in the pot, a little flour for body, water for the liquid, and the potatoes laid on top to steam. Delicious magazine and Ballymaloe add carrots and a stock, and Kerrygold bakes sliced potatoes with butter; none of those are in this version, which stays the plain lamb, onion and potato stew. The ATK page gives no total time; with browning and two hours in the oven this is about 2 hours 20 minutes, so it's a weekend or make-ahead stew rather than a weeknight one.
